summary.oneLiner: Shree Refrigerations is a ~30-year-old refrigeration/test-equipment maker that since 2016-17 became India's premier naval/defence HVAC & refrigeration supplier, claiming **~64% market share** in defence marine AC/REF/HVAC. It is the only Indian firm with "3-of-3" naval registrations — allowed to supply HVAC, AC/REF plant AND its own control panels — and the only firm that indigenized the full submarine (Scorpene) HVAC system. Core thesis = leveraged play on Indian naval fleet expansion (150 → 230 ships), merchant-marine shipbuilding push, and AON pipeline of ₹2.3-2.4 lakh cr (~₹2,500 cr addressable for AC/REF/HVAC at ~1% of project cost), with an optionality kicker in data-centre cooling via Smardt. Guidance: 40% revenue CAGR for 3-5 yrs; ₹1,000 cr revenue / ₹120-130 cr PAT by FY30-31.
summary.business: SRL designs, manufactures, tests, installs and commissions chillers, refrigeration plants, AC plants, turnkey HVAC&R systems and electrical control panels for mission-critical environments, with a heavy concentration in Indian Navy and defence shipbuilding programmes such as the P17A frigates and the Fleet Support Ship. It holds naval registrations across all three of its critical segments and has supplied an award-winning, import-substitute air-conditioning solution for the Scorpene submarine. The company is extending magnetic-bearing chiller technology into India's data-centre cooling market through a technology partnership with Smardt, alongside heavy fabrication services for the defence ecosystem.

currentContext.strategies: Stay a defence-focused, Atmanirbhar-aligned engineering company: deepen the niche naval HVAC&R position by strengthening long-term relationships within the defence ecosystem and expanding execution capabilities across specialised naval applications.|Expand manufacturing capacity through the new Hanbarwadi (Unit 2) greenfield plant with complete backward integration - robotic welding, laser cutting, bending, paint shop, shot blast - to serve existing order commitments and anticipated future business, improve operational efficiency and optimise production costs.|Enter and scale the data-centre cooling vertical, introducing oil-free magnetic bearing chiller technology in India through the Smardt partnership, executed via wholly owned subsidiary Trezor Technologies Private Limited.|Retain integrated in-house execution across engineering, manufacturing, testing, installation and commissioning as the core differentiator, supported by in-house testing infrastructure and formal naval inspection at each stage.|Build the specialised talent pipeline - continuous training, in-house capability building and knowledge retention through the SPACE framework, Great Learning Tuesdays, competency mapping, campus tie-ups with government and technical engineering institutes - as the industry moves toward AI-driven infrastructure.|Grow responsibly: develop the new manufacturing facility to IGBC Green Building standards, adopt energy-efficient systems, and integrate sustainable practices into manufacturing as the company expands, guided by a five-tenet energy management strategy (optimise energy use, adopt new and emerging technologies and digital initiatives, utilise low-grade waste heat, reduce carbon intensity of energy used, optimise cost of energy).|Reinvest rather than distribute - no dividend for FY2025-26 in order to strengthen the financial position and fund future business expansion plans.
currentContext.expansion: FY26 was the company's first major capacity-addition year. During the financial year SRL incurred significant capital expenditure primarily towards establishing a new manufacturing facility, with the stated objective of enhancing production capacity to cater to existing order commitments as well as anticipated future business; total capital expenditure incurred during the year amounted to Rs. 2,437.56 lakhs, financed through a combination of IPO proceeds, term loan and internal accruals. The centrepiece is the second manufacturing facility (Unit 2) at Hanbarwadi in Satara district, Maharashtra - a state-of-the-art greenfield unit developed on 6.5 acres that expands the manufacturing footprint by 50,000 square feet, inaugurated on 20 June 2026 and commencing commercial operations with effect from that date. It is built for complete backward integration and is equipped with robotic welding, laser cutting, bending, a paint shop and modern shot blast; the individual investments listed for the year include installation of a laser cutting machine, a bending machine, heavy-duty cranes and a paint shop at Unit 2, plus construction and installation of a shot blasting shed. Separately the Company renovated its Corporate Office at Unit 1 - Virvade to improve workplace infrastructure and administrative facilities. Management expects these investments to substantially enhance manufacturing capacity, improve operational efficiency, optimise production costs and support long-term strategic objectives. The expansion is framed as a green build - the new manufacturing facility is being developed to meet IGBC Green Building standards with a focus on efficient resource use and responsible construction, alongside energy-efficiency measures and an energy management strategy guided by five tenets, while the Company is still evaluating feasible options for alternate sources of energy (capital investment on energy conservation equipment is not separately indicated as it forms part of other substantive capital assets). Adjacent to the physical build-out, wholly owned subsidiary Trezor Technologies Private Limited entered into an agreement with Smardt Chillers Pte. Ltd., Singapore for the sale, installation and after-sales servicing of chillers to data centres in India, which is expected to strengthen the Company's presence in the data centre cooling segment. The capacity build is backed by a closing order book of over Rs 270 Crore, stated at approximately 1.8x of FY26 revenue.

risks.note: MD&A Risks & Concerns: operations are closely linked to defence procurement timelines, naval project execution schedules and government spending priorities, and delays in approvals, project execution or procurement cycles may impact order inflows and revenue recognition. Mitigation cited is strengthening long-term relationships within the defence ecosystem while expanding execution capabilities across specialised naval applications - it does not reduce the underlying single-customer-ecosystem dependence.

risks.risk: Rapid shifts in Indian defence procurement policy and naval technical specifications
risks.note: Board risk table flags 'Strategic Sector Shifts' - rapid changes in Indian Defence procurement policies or technical specifications for naval platforms - which can strand qualification work in a business where approval cycles are long. Mitigation is active R&D and closer collaboration with defence laboratories to stay aligned.

risks.risk: Volatile refrigerant pricing and component supply-chain pressure
risks.note: MD&A: the industry continues to experience volatility in refrigerant prices driven by global supply-and-demand imbalances, and supply chain disruptions and component shortages can directly impact procurement timelines and project deliveries - i.e. it hits both margin and delivery schedules. Mitigation is diversified sourcing, strategic vendor partnerships and calibrated inventory planning.

risks.risk: Reliance on specialised imported raw materials for production continuity
risks.note: Board risk table rates 'Supply Chain Continuity' as High priority: reliance on specialized raw materials such as high-grade alloys or electronic controllers can lead to production delays. Mitigation is developing an alternate vendor base and increasing in-house fabrication of critical components to reduce dependency on imports and logistical issues.

MD&A: defence-grade cooling systems for defence, marine and data centre applications involve high-order technical complexity, but availability of specialised talent in system design, advanced controls and precision installation remains limited; this talent gap can impact project timelines, service quality and the scalability of operations - a direct constraint on the company's stated capacity expansion.

risks.risk: Inventory carrying value and working-capital intensity
risks.note: The statutory auditor designated 'Valuation of Inventory' a Key Audit Matter, noting inventory forms a significant part of the assets at Rs. 5,477.04 lacs as of 31st March 2026, representing 18.26% of total assets, made up of raw materials, spares and semi-finished goods including steel, pumps and spares managed internally at warehouse. The judgement inherent in valuing that block is a recurring audit-attention item for a project-execution business.

risks.risk: Newly listed SME: IPO proceeds utilisation and reduced governance-disclosure regime
risks.note: The auditor's report carries an Emphasis of Matter drawing attention to the Company's listing on the SME Platform of BSE Limited on 1st August 2025, the consequent changes in share capital structure and the utilisation of IPO proceeds towards the objects of the issue (opinion not modified). FY26 capex was part-funded from those IPO proceeds, so utilisation against stated objects remains a live monitoring item in the company's first year as a listed entity.

risks.risk: External macro and regulatory factors named in the cautionary statement
risks.note: The MD&A cautionary statement enumerates the factors that could make actual results differ materially: economic conditions, government policies, defence procurement cycles, regulatory changes, competition and other external factors - with the company undertaking no obligation to update its forward-looking statements.

segment_detail.title: Segment Detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Defence/marine (core):** AC plants (4 of 6 Navy-standard capacities type-tested), HVAC (ATU all 6 type-tested, AFU/NBC filtration all type-tested, ventilation fans ~70% type-tested), control panels, oil-free compressor chillers. Revenue from new-build, retrofit, spares, and installation/AMC/lifecycle.
- **Spares & service:** Fell to 7% of FY26 revenue (was 30% FY25) — the margin swing factor; target rebuild to 15-20%.
- **Industrial/process cooling & test equipment:** Original 30-yr business; test chambers/equipment for other refrigeration firms.
- **Data centre (new):** Land-based chiller cooling via Smardt tie-up (~6 months old); oil-free/mag-bearing chiller tech same as defence.

order_book.title: Order Book & Pipeline
order_book.body:
- **Closing order book ₹270 cr (31-Mar-26), ~1.8x revenue**; opened FY26 at ₹215 cr (bulk received in last quarter).
- 8 ongoing projects; 4 to complete in FY27, rest spill to FY28.
- Completed flagship: **P17A Nilgiri-class frigate** (oil-free compressor chiller supplied; PM-dedicated) and **Scorpene submarine** HVAC indigenization — both now spares/service annuity sources.
- Shipyards not named individually but customers are India's naval shipyards (GRSE / Mazagon / Cochin / Goa Shipyard implied via coastline offices: Visakhapatnam, Kolkata, Chennai, Goa, Mumbai, Pune, Delhi; Kochi office opening FY26).
- AON pipeline ₹2.3-2.4 lakh cr → ~₹2,500 cr defence-marine TAM for AC/REF/HVAC (~1% of project cost) over 2-2.5 yrs; +₹500 cr non-defence marine → ₹3,000-3,500 cr total marine TAM.
- Hit rate: retrofits ~100%; newbuilds — lost a few tenders (only segment with losses).

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL)
guidance.body:
- **Revenue:** 40% CAGR for next 3-5 years (CMD reaffirmed; CEO noted 50% delivered in FY26). Plant-expansion incremental rev guided at 20% CAGR (CFO) — but headline company guidance is 40%.
- **Long-term target:** ₹1,000 cr revenue and ₹120-130 cr PAT by FY30-31 (reaffirmed; management explicitly stands by ₹1,000 cr "ladder in next 5 years," not the literal ₹833 cr a flat-40% compound would give).
- **EBITDA margin:** 20-24% going forward (CFO); to improve as spares/service mix rebuilds toward 15-20% of revenue.
- **Order inflow (FY27):** ~₹1,000 cr of defence tenders expected to be floated in FY27; win rate depends on competition (current share 64%). ~60 marine tenders expected from Ministry this year.
- **H1/H2 FY27:** Less skewed than FY26 but H2 still larger (driven by shipyard delivery schedules).
- **Data centre:** Reference installation in FY27 (no revenue contribution); meaningful revenue from FY28. FY27 guidance is WITHOUT data centre.
- **Defence/naval mix:** Naval/defence remains core (~bulk of revenue); data centre + merchant marine are additive optionality.

growth_optionality.title: Growth / Optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- Indian Navy fleet 150 → 230 ships over 5-7 yrs; merchant-marine shipbuilding push (top-10 by 2035, top-3/5 by 2047) — Ministry demand aggregation rose 200 → 434 ships, projected ~700.
- Submarine/Scorpene indigenization franchise; only Indian firm with full submarine HVAC indigenization.
- **Data-centre cooling:** cooling = ~12-13% of a DC project; DC cooling market ₹/$2.99 bn → ~$9 bn over 3 yrs (~25-30% CAGR). Smardt channel partnership; reference install FY27, revenue FY28+.
- **Danfoss Turbocor TASP:** only authorized service partner in India for oil-free/mag-bearing compressors (~1,200-1,300 installed base) — strategic capability/annuity build, low near-term revenue.
- **Exports:** nascent, in marine segment only (not data centre); early discussions.
- "3-of-3" registration + turnkey ordering shift by shipyards (AC+HVAC bundled) structurally favors Shree as single-source supplier.

margins.title: Margins & Cost
margins.body:
- FY EBITDA margin 21% (down from 27%) — mix-led (low spares); H2 26.3% on operating leverage as rev doubled with flat employee/other cost.
- Guided 20-24% EBITDA; improvement hinges on spares/service rising to 15-20%.
- Metal/commodity (copper) inflation flagged as "unprecedented" — partly hedged via inflation built into multi-year fixed-price bids, but acknowledged small EBITDA drag going forward.
- Employee cost ₹7 cr → ₹21 cr over 4 yrs; future hiring/other-expense growth to lag revenue growth (operating leverage thesis).

capital_allocation.title: Capital Allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- FY26 IPO: ₹95 cr fresh issue (BSE listing 2025); deployed into capex, debt reduction, working-capital, and yielding interest income.
- Paid off high-cost debt; balance sheet "not leveraged."
- Future growth funded by internal accruals + bank funding (working capital is the main need); no external equity raise flagged for 40-50% CAGR plan.
- Not eligible for BSE/NSE main-board migration for ~2 more years; plans to migrate when window opens.

management_tone.title: Management Tone
management_tone.body: Confident, nationalistic ("we manufacture pride"), aligned to "Amrit Kaal"/PM vision. Delivered ahead of prior 40% guidance (50% achieved). Candid on margin compression (mix), commodity drag, and tender losses in newbuilds. Receptive but firm on NOT moving to quarterly reporting (argues annual/half-yearly more accurate for defence cycle) while promising more frequent commentary. Reaffirmed ₹1,000 cr / ₹120-130 cr PAT FY30-31 target without hedging.

risks.title: Risks
risks.body:
- **Defence-order lumpiness / H1-H2 skew** — driven by shipyard delivery schedules; numbers misleading on quarterly basis (mgmt resists quarterly reporting, prefers H1/annual).
- **Working capital** still high at 370 days despite improvement; GST input-credit lock-up (₹19.9 cr other current assets) until refund.
- **Commodity (copper/metal) inflation** beyond bid assumptions on multi-year fixed-price contracts.
- Customer concentration on Indian Navy / shipyards; newbuild tender losses.
- Data-centre & exports unproven (no revenue yet); execution dependent on partner (Smardt) product qualification.
- Single-listing (BSE) / small-cap liquidity; main-board migration gated 2 yrs.

non_obvious.title: Non-Obvious Points
non_obvious.body:
- Margin drop is a FEATURE of revenue surge (spares share mechanically diluted by booming equipment deliveries), not deterioration — spares is the high-margin annuity that rebuilds as completed platforms (P17A, Scorpene) age into retrofit/AMC.
- "1% of project cost" rule-of-thumb makes Shree a clean derivative of total naval/marine capex without bidding for whole platforms.
- Turnkey-ordering shift by shipyards is a quiet moat-widener: rivals who supply only AC OR HVAC must partner; Shree is single-source.
- Danfoss TASP and Smardt tie-ups are capability/optionality plays (low revenue now) but position Shree for the same oil-free chiller tech across defence + data centre + pharma.
- Working-capital compression (570→370 days) is as material to the equity story as revenue growth — funds the 40% CAGR off internal accruals.

qoq_log.title: QoQ / Period Log
qoq_log.body: - **H2 & FY26 (call 26-May-2026):** First full earnings call post-FY26. Rev ₹153 cr (+50% YoY), PAT ₹21 cr (+64%), EPS ₹6.47 (+28% despite IPO dilution). Order book ₹270 cr (1.8x). WC 570→370 days. EBITDA 21% (mix-led drop from 27%); guided 20-24% fwd. Reaffirmed 40% rev CAGR (3-5 yr) and ₹1,000 cr / ₹120-130 cr PAT FY30-31. Hanbarwadi ₹25 cr capex live June-26 (~₹400 cr peak rev capacity). New: Smardt DC-cooling tie-up (rev FY28+), Danfoss Turbocor TASP, Kochi office, export exploration (marine). IPO ₹95 cr fresh issue completed FY26; main-board migration ~2 yrs out.
